sections.label: SAF anti-terror priority
sections.summary: Asked how the SAF adds anti-terror operations to its priorities, the Minister notes no specific intelligence but a three-fold rise in ISIS-related attacks in ASEAN since 2013.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: asked	the Minister for Defence how is the SAF adding anti-terror operations to their priority, in addition to securing Singapore's sovereignty.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: While we do not have any specific intelligence on any impending plot targeted at Singapore, the number of Islamic State of Iraq and Syria (ISIS)-related attacks in surrounding ASEAN countries and other regions since 2013 has increased three-fold in the last four years.

sections.label: SAF offers to Philippines
sections.summary: The Minister visited the Philippines and Secretary Lorenzana accepted in principle SAF offers of humanitarian supplies, use of urban training villages, and a UAV detachment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: I visited the Philippines two weeks ago, where I thanked Philippine Secretary of National Defense Delfin Lorenzana and the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) for their decisive action in Mindanao and Marawi City.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: We discussed ways in which the SAF could help the AFP concretely and Secretary Lorenzana has accepted in principle our offers of: one, humanitarian supplies for the evacuees from Marawi, this will be flown in via the Republic of Singapore Air Force's C-130 transport aircraft; two, the use of the SAF's urban training villages for AFP troops to be trained in counter-terror; and three, a detachment of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles to enhance the AFP's intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance capabilities.

sections.label: IDTI homeland security training
sections.summary: From July this year, the IDTI will train approximately 18,000 soldiers from active and NS units yearly in homeland security operations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: From July this year, the IDTI will train approximately 18,000 soldiers from active and NS units yearly in homeland security operations.

sections.label: Exercise Highcrest MSTF
sections.summary: The Singapore Navy's MSTF will lead Exercise Highcrest in October this year, with whole-of-Government agencies participating.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: The Singapore Navy's MSTF will lead Exercise Highcrest in October this year, with the participation of whole-of-Government agencies.

sections.label: Counter-terrorism office and command system
sections.summary: The Defence Technology Community set up a dedicated Counter-Terrorism office in DSTA in October last year, and a common Command and Control Information System now enables SAF and Home Team joint operations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Lastly, the Defence Technology Community has set up a dedicated Counter-Terrorism office in the Defence Science and Technology Agency (DSTA) in October last year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Joint operations between the SAF and the Home Team are now enabled by a common Command and Control Information System, which provides situational awareness and interoperability.

sections.label: Joint command and control system
sections.summary: The Minister says a joint Command and Control Information System developed by DSTA, used by the Home Team and SAF, shares the same picture and helps divide or combine responsibilities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: But how do you make sure that while they are responding, the SAF also is keenly aware of what happens to them?

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: That is why I talked about a joint system now, a Command and Control Information System, which both the Home Team and the SAF now use, which was developed by DSTA so that you share the same picture and that makes a lot of difference, as well as having an understanding of when you can divide out responsibilities, when you can actually come together.

sections.label: Multinational effort in Philippines
sections.summary: Contributions to the Philippines do not amount to a multinational effort because there is no central or prime mover.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Is Singapore's contribution part of a multinational effort?

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: So far, the contributions to the Philippines do not lend themselves to that sense of a multinational effort because there is no central or prime mover for that.

sections.label: Singapore assisting against entrenching terrorism
sections.summary: Singapore thought it right to assist because entrenched terrorist cells would subject ASEAN cities to attacks.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: We have good relations with the AFP and there is good personal contact between myself and Secretary Lorenzana.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: And we thought that it was right for Singapore to assist because, if this problem becomes entrenched and it gets worse, cities in ASEAN will bear the brunt and will be subject to attacks if these terrorist cells become entrenched there.

sections.label: Training National Servicemen in IDTI
sections.summary: In the IDTI, 18,000 National Servicemen are trained every year to do the rudiments.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The better trained they are, the better they are equipped, the more confident they are.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: So, in the IDTI, we are training 18,000 National Servicemen every year to do the rudiments.

sections.label: SAF basic search training
sections.summary: Simulations teach proper search, so SAF resources are trained at basic level for multiple attacks.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: We have various simulations on how to do a proper search, which, traditionally, they were not trained for because the Home Team is better at it.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: But in the event that you have multiple attacks and you need the resources of the SAF, then at least, at the very least, you have them trained at the basic level.

sections.label: Rapidity of lone wolf attacks
sections.summary: Small group and lone wolf attacks are rapid and must be dealt with before formal security agencies mobilise.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Because the problem with small group and lone wolf attacks is the rapidity of these attacks.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: And you have to deal with the situation before formal security agencies can mobilise.
